features.name: GATE — agisdk + GLM, one task end to end
features.description: [GATE] Run exactly one REAL task end to end with GLM through z.ai and get a score back. This feature exists to answer three questions that the plan could not resolve from documentation, and each answer must be written into docs/DECISIONS.md: (1) does agisdk accept a custom OpenAI-compatible base_url, so z.ai's GLM can drive it? agisdk depends on openai>=1.0.0, which suggests yes, but that is inference and not evidence. (2) Are the 11 replica sites served locally, or hosted at realevals.xyz? This decides how much of the speed gain from leaving the live web is actually realised. (3) Does local scoring require a leaderboard key? STOP AND REPORT if GLM cannot be wired up. Do not silently switch to a paid OpenAI or Anthropic model — that changes the project's cost profile and its subject, and it is a scoping decision for a human. Done when: one task runs, a score is returned, and all three questions are answered with recorded evidence.

features.name: Agent loop with caps
features.description: The loop: observe, decide, act, repeat, terminate. Explicit caps on steps, tokens and wall-clock, each configurable and each recorded when hit. INHERITED LESSON, do not rediscover it: per-operation timeouts are NOT a bound on the whole operation — the archived predecessor sat on one site for nine minutes with every sub-timeout at 45s or less. Only a wall-clock race bounds an action. Done when: each cap can be demonstrated firing independently, the reason for termination is recorded per episode, and hitting a cap ends the episode cleanly rather than hanging.
features.verification: `uv run pytest -q -k caps` — the step, token and wall-clock caps each fire in isolation and end the episode cleanly, and the stored episode record names which cap terminated it. A hang is a failure, so the wall-clock case must assert on elapsed time, not just on the return value.

features.name: Task runner over the 112, with resume
features.description:
Batch runner across REAL's task set, plus the supervisor that drives it unattended. MUST CHECKPOINT AND RESUME: the archived predecessor lost an eight-hour run that produced nothing because it could not resume after a failure. A task already completed is never re-run on resume, and the runner states how many it skipped. One task's failure never aborts the batch.

THE RULES ARE IN docs/DECISIONS.md ENTRY 7, decided before this feature exists because none of them can be applied honestly after seeing the results. Implement them, do not re-litigate them:
(a) runs/<run-id>/manifest.json is written before the first task and never edited — the task ids, the population they were drawn from (112 / 102 / 47, see entry 5), and every exclusion with its reason.
(b) One atomically-written record per task (tmp file + os.replace, so a kill mid-write cannot corrupt one). Terminal statuses: passed, failed, capped, errored. Each record carries reward, steps, tokens, wall-clock, and which cap fired if one did.
(c) A provider error (429, 401, entitlement change, reset) is NOT a task failure and NOT terminal — status provider_error, the task stays unattempted, and it is retryable. Recording provider errors as zero-reward failures is how an unattended run publishes a wrong success rate.
(d) runs/<run-id>/results.tsv is append-only, one row per ATTEMPT including retries. The rate is computed from each task's FIRST terminal attempt; retries exist to survive interruptions, never to re-roll a task until it passes.
(e) scripts/supervise.py re-invokes the runner until one of three machine-checkable outcomes and never runs unbounded: exit 0 every manifest task terminal; exit 1 stalled, K consecutive rounds added no new terminal record; exit 2 token or wall-clock budget exceeded. Idempotent — re-running after a completed run prints the summary and changes nothing. Each round logs what it attempted, what became terminal, and any backoff.

(f) CONCURRENCY, per entry 7's second half: --concurrency N, DEFAULT 3, because z.ai publishes a per-model concurrency limit and for glm-4.6 it is 3. This machine (10 cores, 64 GB) is not the constraint — an episode is model-bound, 9 model calls over 35 s in the gate. Workers are PROCESSES, not threads: agisdk drives Playwright's sync API, which has thread affinity. No two concurrent episodes on the same site until state isolation is measured — REAL scores by diffing environment state, and a shared server-side site would contaminate both diffs. A concurrency-limit rejection is a provider_error under (c), never a task failure, and the supervisor halves concurrency on one and recovers slowly. The manifest records the concurrency level, because per-task wall-clock at N=3 is not comparable to sequential.

BEFORE THE FULL RUN: the published limit of 3 is for the pay-as-you-go API and this key is a Coding Plan key — probe 2, 3, 4 and 5 concurrent trivial completions, record which are rejected and with what code, and write the measured number into docs/DECISIONS.md. Do NOT switch to glm-4.5 or glm-5.1 for their higher limits; that changes the subject of the measurement and is a human decision.

SCOPE: no worktree isolation, no separate methodology file (AGENTS.md and these fields are it), and no model in the supervision path — the evaluator is agisdk's programmatic checks.
features.verification:
Four checks, all of which must have run:
(1) `uv run pytest -q -k 'resume or supervise'` passes.
(2) KILL TEST: a real batch is killed mid-run with SIGKILL (not a clean exit) and restarted — the second run reports how many tasks it skipped, re-runs none of them, loses no recorded result, and finishes. Paste both runs' output.
(3) STALL TEST: point the runner at an endpoint that returns 429 (a bogus key reproduces this — entry 4 shows the exact responses) and confirm the supervisor exits 1 as stalled, having written ZERO terminal records. A provider outage must not produce failures.
(4) BUDGET TEST: set a token or wall-clock budget the run cannot meet and confirm exit 2, mid-run, with every already-terminal record intact.
Also: `results.tsv` has one row per attempt with retries visible, and re-running `supervise.py` on a completed run is a no-op that changes no file.

features.name: Evaluation and cost recording
features.description: Score via agisdk's own programmatic checks rather than a reimplementation, so the number stays comparable to REAL's published baseline. Record TOKENS PER TASK from the provider's usage numbers, summed from actual responses rather than estimated. A dollar figure ONLY if z.ai publishes rates for this plan — if it does not, record that it does not and report tokens alone. The sibling project hit this exact question and correctly refused to invent a rate. Done when: a small batch produces per-task pass/fail plus per-task token counts, and the aggregate is reproducible from the stored per-task records.
features.verification: A small batch produces per-task pass/fail and per-task token counts from the provider's usage numbers, and the aggregate recomputes from the stored per-task records alone (rerun the aggregation over `runs/<id>/` and get the same figure). A dollar figure appears only if z.ai publishes a rate for this plan; if it does not, docs/DECISIONS.md records that it does not.

features.name: Ablation — observation richness
features.description: Run the task set at two observation richness levels and report the difference in success rate. This is the argument for the whole migration: REAL's sites are deterministic, so both arms see byte-identical pages and the difference between them is the thing you changed — on the live web, page variance between arms would have been a confounder sitting on top of the effect. Report both arms with their n, and state the comparison honestly if the difference is small or zero. Done when: both arms have run over the same task set and the delta is recorded with both raw numbers.
features.verification: Both arms have run over the same task set, at richness levels that differ only in the serializer parameter, and docs/DECISIONS.md records both raw success rates with their n and the delta between them — stated honestly if the delta is small or zero.
